correctness.rationale: For the MDS dual of dimension \(n-k\), projection surjectivity gives dimension of checks supported on T exactly \(\max\{|T|-k,0\}\). A vertex separator S of size below k would constrain all parity checks to two supported subspaces whose summed dimension is strictly below \(n-k\), impossible. Simplicial deletion preserves k-connectivity in chordal graphs; puncturing preserves MDS, and a supported check through the deleted vertex extends an inductive spanning set. Every edge lies in a \((k+1)\)-clique, giving exact primal realization over the original field. Minimum degree k at each simplicial peel gives \(kn-\binom{k+1}{2}\) edges with equality precisely for \(k\)-trees; their \(n-k\) creation-clique checks are a dual basis. A finite modular verifier independently checks 180 \(k\)-trees, all 480 dual bases of an example and every qualifying labeled graph on four to six vertices; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The recently introduced chordal-code framework motivates representing one fixed code with minimal coordinate-interaction complexity. The theorem supplies the entire admissible chordal graph family, a sharp universal interaction-edge lower bound and characterization of every minimizing topology, valid for all fields and all MDS dimensions (including boundary cases). These are structural design and obstruction results beyond an example, code-construction recipe, or minor numerical improvement. It does not assert actual decoding-runtime gains or hardware superiority.
